questions.stem: A man walks 5 m north, then 3 m east. His final distance from the starting point is:
questions.explanation: Net N-S = 5, net E-W = 3. Pythagoras: √(25 + 9) = √34 ≈ 5.83 m. Single-step Pythagoras item.

questions.stem: Starting from her house, Priya walks 6 km east, then 8 km north, then 3 km west, then 4 km south. Her straight-line distance from home is:
questions.explanation: Net E-W = 6 − 3 = 3 east. Net N-S = 8 − 4 = 4 north. Pythagoras: √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 km. Uses the (3, 4, 5) triple.

questions.stem: A girl travels from A: 3 km north, 4 km east, 9 km south, 8 km west, then 6 km north. Her straight-line distance from A is:
questions.explanation: Net N-S = 3 − 9 + 6 = 0. Net E-W = 4 − 8 = −4 (i.e., 4 km west of A). Straight-line distance from A = 4 km.

questions.stem: Ravi starts facing north. He turns right and walks 5 km; then right again, walks 8 km; then left and walks 3 km; then left and walks 5 km. His final position relative to the start is:

options.option_text: √73 km (≈ 8.54 km), to the south-east; he faces north
10 km due east; he faces north
8 km due west; he faces east

questions.explanation: Track position step by step from (0,0) facing N. Turn R → face E, walk 5 → (5,0). Turn R → face S, walk 8 → (5,−8). Turn L → face E, walk 3 → (8,−8). Turn L → face N, walk 5 → (8,−3). End at (8, −3) facing N. Distance = √(64+9) = √73 ≈ 8.54 km to the south-east of start.

questions.stem: Ravi starts from point X facing south. He walks 4 m, turns left, walks 3 m, turns left, walks 4 m. In which direction is he from X?
questions.explanation: Start (0,0) facing S. Walk 4 S → (0,−4). Turn L (from S = E). Walk 3 E → (3,−4). Turn L (from E = N). Walk 4 N → (3,0). He's at (3, 0) — 3 m EAST of X.
